'''''Parietaria debilis''''', commonly known as '''pellitory''', '''small-flower pellitory''',<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Lee |editor1-first=Sangtae |editor2-last=Chang |editor2-first=Kae Sun |title=English Names for Korean Native Plants |year=2015 |publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]] |location=Pocheon |isbn=978-89-97450-98-5 |page=561 |url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf |access-date=22 March 2019 |via=[[Korea Forest Service]] |archive-date=25 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170525105020/http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> or '''native pellitory''', is a herb native to [[Australia]] and [[New Zealand]].

==Description==
It grows as an annual herb from 7 to 40 centimetres in height, with green or white flowers. Individual plants bear both [[perfect flower|perfect]] and [[imperfect flower|imperfect]] flowers.<ref name="FloraBase 1762">{{FloraBase | name = ''Parietaria debilis'' G.Forst. | id = 1762}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
This species was published in 1786 by [[Georg Forster]], based on a type specimen collected in New Zealand. It has twice been moved to other genera—to ''[[Urtica]]'' by [[Stephan Endlicher]] in 1833, and to ''[[Freirea]]'' by [[Alexander Viktorovich Jarmolenko]] in 1941—but neither move was accepted.<ref name="APNI 43051">{{APNI | name = ''Parietaria debilis'' G.Forst | id = 43051}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is native to Australia and New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora_details.aspx?ID=2214 |title=Parietaria debilis |website=www.nzpcn.org.nz |access-date=18 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://florabase.dpaw.wa.gov.au/browse/profile/1762 |title=Parietaria debilis G.Forst. Pellitory |website=florabase.dpaw.wa.gov.au |language=en |access-date=18 May 2019 |archive-date=12 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170212030927/https://florabase.dpaw.wa.gov.au/browse/profile/1762 |url-status=live }}</ref> In Australia it is widespread in temperate regions, occurring in every state and territory.<ref name="APNI 43051"/> It favours well-drained sites, especially in calcareous soils.<ref name="FloraBase 1762"/><ref name="PlantNET">{{NSW Flora Online | genus = Parietaria | species = debilis | author = G.Forst}}</ref>

== Research ==
DNA was able to be extracted, and the chloroplast DNA trnL–trnF intergenic spacer and trnL intron were sequenced, from a herbarium specimen of ''Parietaria debilis'' collected by Joseph Banks and Daniel Solander on Captain James Cook’s first voyage in 1769–70.<ref>{{CiteQ|Q106839643}}</ref>
